subject: geom_abline not showing in all panels

messages.author: 8eec65cdf68e8c8f
messages.subject: geom_abline not showing in all panels
parts:
Hi,

I'm not sure if it's a bug and if bug reports should be posted on this mailing list or on github,
but I have a problem getting an geom_abline to show in all panels when there are multiple layers with different data and each data has one level of the factor that is used to split up the data into panels:

library(ggplot2)
data(mtcars)

# Add grouping variable to data
data <- mtcars;
data$group <- ifelse(data$cyl == 4, "GR2", "GR1")

# Split data into colored and gray points
dataCol <- subset(data, group == "GR1")
dataGray <- subset(data, group == "GR2")

ggplot(dataCol, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, color = as.factor(cyl))) +
geom_point() +
geom_point(data = dataGray, mapping = aes(color = NA), color = "#666666") +
geom_abline(intercept = 10, slope = 3) +
facet_grid(group ~ .)

If I've read the docs right, the abline should be shown in all panels, doesn't it?

As a workaround, using the same abline parameters for both groups works:

dataAbline <- data.frame(a = 10, b = 3, group = c("GR1", "GR2"))

ggplot(dataCol, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, color = as.factor(cyl))) +
geom_point() +
geom_point(data = dataGray, mapping = aes(color = NA), color = "#666666") +
geom_abline(data = dataAbline, mapping = aes(intercept = a, slope = b)) +
facet_grid(group ~ .)

Best regards,
David

> library(ggplot2)
> data(mtcars)
>
> # Add grouping variable to data
> data <- mtcars;
> data$group <- ifelse(data$cyl == 4, "GR2", "GR1")
>
> # Split data into colored and gray points
> dataCol <- subset(data, group == "GR1")
> dataGray <- subset(data, group == "GR2")
>
> ggplot(dataCol, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, color = as.factor(cyl))) +
> geom_point() +
> geom_point(data = dataGray, mapping = aes(color = NA), color = "#666666") +
> geom_abline(intercept = 10, slope = 3) +
> facet_grid(group ~ .)
>
> If I've read the docs right, the abline should be shown in all panels,
> doesn't it?

I don't think so. The default data for the plot is dataCol, so that is
the dataset used by geom_abline. More generally, splitting the data
into subsets and plotting each one separately is rarely the best way.
Here is how I would go about this:

ggplot(data, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, color = as.factor(cyl))) +
geom_point() +

aes(x = wt, y = mpg, color = as.factor(cyl))) +
geom_point() +

> As a workaround, using the same abline parameters for both groups works:
>
> dataAbline <- data.frame(a = 10, b = 3, group = c("GR1", "GR2"))
>
> ggplot(dataCol, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, color = as.factor(cyl))) +
> geom_point() +
> geom_point(data = dataGray, mapping = aes(color = NA), color = "#666666") +
> geom_abline(data = dataAbline, mapping = aes(intercept = a, slope = b)) +
> facet_grid(group ~ .)

ggplot(dataCol, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, color = as.factor(cyl))) +
geom_point() +
geom_point(data = dataGray, mapping = aes(color = NA), color = "#666666") +

geom_abline(data = data, mapping = aes(intercept = 10, slope = 3)) +
facet_grid(group ~ .)

will also work, but again I would avoid the subsetting approach if possible.

Best,
Ista

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: geom_abline not showing in all panels
parts:
Hi:

Since my solution to this was almost identical to Ista's first
solution, I'll focus on why your code didn't work.

On Sat, Feb 1, 2014 at 6:00 AM, dkep <dkep...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi,
>
> I'm not sure if it's a bug and if bug reports should be posted on this
> mailing list or on github,
> but I have a problem getting an geom_abline to show in all panels when there
> are multiple layers with different data and each data has one level of the
> factor that is used to split up the data into panels:
>
> library(ggplot2)
> data(mtcars)
>
> # Add grouping variable to data
> data <- mtcars;
> data$group <- ifelse(data$cyl == 4, "GR2", "GR1")
>
> # Split data into colored and gray points
> dataCol <- subset(data, group == "GR1")
> dataGray <- subset(data, group == "GR2")
>
> ggplot(dataCol, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, color = as.factor(cyl))) +
> geom_point() +
> geom_point(data = dataGray, mapping = aes(color = NA), color = "#666666") +
> geom_abline(intercept = 10, slope = 3) +
> facet_grid(group ~ .)
>
> If I've read the docs right, the abline should be shown in all panels,
> doesn't it?

Nope. This is a consequence of the training process that takes place
when a ggplot is constructed. In a nutshell, the reason you didn't get
a line in your second panel is because dataGray was not 'visible' to
geom_abline(). Notice the difference between the data in your base
layer (dataCol) and that in Ista's code (data). By default, geoms
refer to the data in the base layer unless otherwise instructed. This
is why, in your code, geom_abline() was rendered in the first panel
(associated with dataCol) and not the second (dataGray).

Considering that group is a character vector in both dataCol and
dataGray with different (single) values in each data frame, you should
find it a remarkable achievement that ggplot() was smart enough to do
the proper faceting.

BTW, since dataCol only contained 6 and 8 cylinder cars, when you
defined the color aesthetic as factor(cyl), the legend only contained
those two values because, once again, it looked to the base layer for
the information. If you take out the scale_color_hue() line from
Ista's code, you'll find that the legend will contain 4, 6 and 8 as
values, because all three of those values are in the full data frame.

The bottom line is that you have to be careful when adding layers to a
ggplot with data frames different from the one defined in the base
layer. The basics of the training process are described in Chapter 3
of the ggplot2 book.

Dennis

>
> As a workaround, using the same abline parameters for both groups works:
>
> dataAbline <- data.frame(a = 10, b = 3, group = c("GR1", "GR2"))
>
> ggplot(dataCol, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, color = as.factor(cyl))) +
> geom_point() +
> geom_point(data = dataGray, mapping = aes(color = NA), color = "#666666") +
> geom_abline(data = dataAbline, mapping = aes(intercept = a, slope = b)) +
> facet_grid(group ~ .)

> Best regards,
> David

Hi,

thank you both for the very quick and thorough responses! I know splitting the data up was a very ugly solution, but I was too dumb to see the easy ways out :)

It was actually intended that the legend doesn't show the gray group, that's why I went through all the struggles.

I think I'll use Ista's second approach as it is the most natural one for my original problem!

Thanks,
David
